name: How do you match existing molding profiles during a repair?

mainEntity.name: How do you match existing molding profiles during a repair?

acceptedAnswer.text: Matching existing molding requires checking its exact material, thickness, height, and edge profile. Standard baseboard or casing from modern builds can often be matched with off-the-shelf stock from local suppliers, while older Denver homes may feature custom or discontinued profiles. When exact duplicates are not available in stores, a contractor can take a physical sample, mill custom stock, or use a multi-piece trim buildup using standard components to replicate the original look. Homeowners should remove or photograph a clean cross-section of the damaged molding before shopping for replacements.
acceptedAnswer.description: Contractors match trim by taking a clean cross-section sample to check against local lumber stock, milling a custom profile, or combining standard profiles to recreate the design.
